newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH CLUBS MOVE TO AVOID STRIKE ACTION OVER NEW YEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH CLUBS MOVE TO AVOID STRIKE ACTION OVER NEW YEAR.

text.p: Spanish first division clubs proposed on Friday to move games scheduled for December 29 to February 19 next year in a bid to head off the threat of a players' strike.
"We'll take this to a happy ending," said Atletico Madrid president Jesus Gil after the meeting.
'The players should enjoy their Christmas and then accept the burden of the games they will have."

Players angry at losing their traditional New Year break had talked of strike action and proposed several other dates. The move, if accepted by Spain's Association of Professional Footballers, will mean re-scheduling several Spanish Cup games.

Meanwhile in Valladolid Spanish national team manager Javier Clemente has lashed out at the country's top sports officals after they claimed he had not done enough to ensure that Spain retained their Olympic soccer title in Atlanta.

"The sports politicians only think of medals," said Clemente on Friday. "It's shameful that now they should complain of bad organisation in the Olympic competition, when they didn't even come to see us play."

Clemente's earlier comments -- seen by many as an excuse for the 4-0 quarter-final defeat by Argentina -- had earned him a rebuke from Alfredo Goyoeneche, vice-president of the Spanish Olympic Committee.
The ever-controversial Clemente re-stated his belief that adequate preparation for the Olympics was incompatible with the obligations placed on players by the clubs.
"I believe it's more important that the team is well prepared during the season than to win a medal," he said.
